appraisal_events.evidence: "pour ne pas confondre vous demanderez si c'est la voiture de la marquise de Villeparisis... elle a deux chevaux" / "C'était cela que je voulais qu'elle sût pour prendre une grande idée de moi" / "j'éprouvai un grand apaisement"
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator deliberately invokes Mme de Villeparisis's title and two-horse carriage to raise his own standing in the eyes of the fisher-girl, and the retrospective narration frames the resulting relief with knowing, slightly self-mocking language ("cette prise de force de son esprit, cette possession immatérielle") that keeps the reader at a small ironic distance from the young narrator's vanity.

status_effects.explanation: Invoking Mme de Villeparisis's rank momentarily eases the narrator's anxiety about being forgotten and gives him a self-perceived (if immaterial and unverified) sense of having made an impression, a modest local gain rather than a full consummation.

ambiguities: The addressee of the narrator's gesture, the unnamed 'pêcheuse'/'belle fille', is not on the reference sheet as a reviewed individuated figure and is therefore not tracked as a character_present, even though she is the passage's central dramatic focus; the narrator's sense of having 'pleased' her is presented only through his own uncertain, retrospective perception ('il me semblait').
